topic: The first vaccine: Edward Jenner, Berkeley, Gloucestershire, England — on 14 May 1796 he inoculated 8-year-old James Phipps with cowpox matter from milkmaid Sarah Nelmes's hand, later challenged him with smallpox without effect, and coined 'vaccine' from vacca (Latin, cow). Smallpox killed about 30 % of those infected; the WHO declared it eradicated in 1980, the only human disease eradicated. Earlier variolation (China, Ottoman Empire) used smallpox itself and is not a vaccine.
policy_note: Every spoken or shown fact → a claim with ≥ 2 independent publishers; core claims need a primary/scholarly source.

myths.reality: Pasteur developed later vaccines (rabies, 1885) and named the technique in Jenner's honour; the first vaccine was Jenner's cowpox inoculation of 1796 in England.
China and the Ottoman world practised variolation — inoculation with smallpox itself, which was risky; Jenner's method used the harmless cowpox virus and is the first vaccine.
